fields.dct:description: A homogeneous steady state of two reacting chemicals that is stable without diffusion can become unstable to spatial perturbations when the chemicals diffuse at different rates, spontaneously producing a pattern.
fields.dct:source: Alan Turing (1952) The chemical basis of morphogenesis
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: two species, smooth kinetics, linearization about a homogeneous steady state, fixed domain without growth or mechanics. Formal status: the linear instability conditions are proved; existence and stability of nonlinear patterns are proved for many specific models but not in general.
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Measure the reaction Jacobian and the diffusivities of a candidate morphogen pair independently, check that the inequality holds, and then confirm that perturbing the diffusivity ratio switches patterning on or off.
fields.rdfs:label: Turing diffusion-driven instability
